rules: Return aggregations over 3 to 10 day windows all failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.29 to 0.81) even when divided by a 45 to 84 day vol; every return-sum that was accepted used a window of 42 days or longer.
252-day lookbacks came back at ~0.87 coverage on both $roa and $dollar_volume, so 252 is not survivable on this island; 189 was the longest window that passed, treat it as the ceiling.

Two fundamental fields multiplied together ($roe * $book_per_share) landed exactly on the coverage line, while the fundamental that scored 2.108 used one field over a price field; keep to at most one fundamental per expression.
Four crossovers picked a bare $volume as one parent and inherited a single node; pick parents that both carry a multi-node subtree, not a raw field leaf.

Retuning one constant or one price field of an archived expression is not novelty: EMA 42 for EMA 10, range window 63 for 21, and $high for $close inside TS_MAX were all caught as subtree overlap or rho >= 0.91.

Changing the normalizer under an unchanged numerator gave rho 0.996 (TS_STD versus TS_SUM(ABS) over TS_SUM($return, 63)); novelty has to come from the numerator's field or sign structure, not the denominator.
The stochastic / range-position template ($close against TS_MIN and TS_MAX of the same window) lost three proposals this round to duplicate and correlation; stop sampling that shape here.

Fitness clustered at 1.97 to 3.64 where two widely separated windows were ratioed or two CS_RANKs of different signal families were multiplied; single-window distance-from-high and IF-gated regime switches scored ~0.42 and are already covered.
